Staying on budget during a remodel has less to do with what you pick and more to do with when you decide. Projects usually go over because of small changes made along the way: a layout that shifts after work starts, a material swapped mid-project, a selection left open until the last minute. Each one adds cost and time. The fix is mostly done before day one. Plan the layout first, finalize your selections before work begins, and look at everything together so there are no surprises once the crew is on site. From the owner
Can you add square footage to an existing house that's from the 1950s? Yup. We do it every day at Light Box Homes. Check out this current addition project where we are adding a master bedroom suite to a cute-n-cuddly 1950s bungalow in Decatur. In addition to the addition, we've gutted the kitchen so we can replace any old or rotting wood, level the structure and bring it back to life with new flooring, cabinets, countertops and appliances: A brand new kitchen in addition to the brand new master ensuite. Many ranch and bungalow homes in the Northeast Atlanta area were built as long ago as the 1940s, some even older. Does that mean they're too old to renovate or add on to? Nope. In fact, they're some of the best-built homes on the block! And with the right design+build team at the helm of your home renovation project, these venerable old homes can gain a new lease on life AND additional square footage that can be applied to enlarging a kitchen, adding or expanding a master bedroom suite, or increasing living or storage space. With eleven years renovating and adding on to old homes in the Chamblee area, Light Box Homes can accurately assess your home's ability to 'bulk up,' which allows you to keep the home (and mortgage) that you already have instead of selling and slogging through the real estate market. But it's important to know if your lot conditions are ideal for creating an addition, so give us a call and let's chat!

Heated Bathroom Floors for Utah Winters Cold tile on a winter morning is no fun. Heated bathroom floors fix that with heating cables that sit under the tile and warm it from below. You set the temperature on a wall thermostat, and the floor is warm when you wake up. Radiant heated floors also help the room dry faster after a shower, which means less moisture left behind. The best time to add them is during a remodel, when the old floor is already out. As a Schluter certified team, we install schluter heated floors with the waterproofing and tile as one system, so everything works together and lasts. They work under most tile. Want heated floors Utah winters cannot beat? Masterix Builders offers free estimates on every project.

Can You Move the Sink, Stove, or Refrigerator During a Kitchen Remodel? Do you like the idea of remodeling your kitchen but feel stuck with the current layout? Many homeowners in Woodland, CA assume the sink, stove, or refrigerator has to stay exactly where it is because of existing plumbing, gas lines, or electrical connections. That can make an outdated kitchen feel impossible to improve. The problem usually becomes more frustrating when appliances interrupt traffic flow, prep space feels awkward, or family members constantly get in each other’s way while cooking. The biggest concern is often the same: “Can these appliances actually be moved without creating a huge problem?” In many cases, yes. At McEwin Construction, we provide full kitchen remodeling services in Woodland, Davis, Sacramento, and nearby areas. Our team can redesign your kitchen layout and handle the plumbing, gas, and electrical adjustments needed to relocate sinks, stoves, refrigerators, and other appliances when the project allows. That gives you more flexibility to create a kitchen with better movement, more usable counter space, improved storage, and a layout that fits the way you actually cook and live. We can also complete the rest of the remodel, including cabinets, countertops, flooring, backsplash, lighting, and finishing work. Your old kitchen layout does not always have to define your new one. Contact McEwin Construction today for a FREE estimate.

This three-season room was built onto an existing home, and one of the most important parts of the project was making the new space feel like it belonged there. The interior window finish was matched to the windows throughout the original home. The trim was matched to the home’s existing trim. Even the brick became part of the room rather than something that feels left over from the old exterior. And underneath it all: heated floors to make those cooler Buffalo days a whole lot more comfortable. Spaces like this don't happen by accident. They come from thoughtful planning, the right materials, and a general contractor who understands how light, texture, and layout work together. Fall is a popular time for indoor projects here in Western New York, and our schedule fills up fast once the weather turns. If you've been searching for a home remodeling contractor in North Tonawanda or Buffalo, now is a smart time to start the conversation. Reach out to TBrothers Renovations to book your consultation and start planning a space you'll love coming home to.
